report:
Reviewed the complete symbol_keyed_interfaces claim and all five ordinary implementation associations after adding missing field/member/owner-helper associations. The public boundary requirement is visible in LocalFnSym::sig and body, LocalStructSym::sig and fields, LocalTraitSym::sig and items, and LocalImplSym::sig and items: each accepts its definition symbol plus the database; none accepts an ambient caller scope or inference context. Each checking root derives its resolver from self.scope(db), derives CST from the same definition, and creates its checking context locally. Function owner environment is derived by open_owner from the symbol's owner, including the no-owner case, trait Self and generics, and impl self type and predicates; method-local parameters and predicates extend that environment. Function bodies import their own completed signature and construct their local inference context separately.

Signatures are the primary semantic product: function signatures return Binder<FnSig> containing parameters, result, receiver, and parameter environment without checking cst.body. The captured trait and impl signatures likewise lower their headers rather than member bodies. The narrow-product qualification is satisfied by StructFields and TraitItems/ImplItems. fields derives generic scope from self.sig, checks only field types, and returns a field-specific product. items invokes the captured lower_items helper with source, generics, and owner derived within its public symbol-keyed root. This private helper is not a public checking query: its extra context parameters do not violate the public API rule. It constructs an owned binder of typed member identities, distinguishing function/type/constant and repeated names through occurrence keys. Its keyed lowering creates member symbols with the owning scope; it does not call member body checking. The impl associated-type-value query also takes definition symbols and reads a requested type value rather than function bodies. Coarse CST reads/copies are not consumption of checked bodies as semantic interfaces, consistent with the captured architectural rationale.

Bodies and checking temporaries remain separate from these interface return products. The function body query is a distinct requested root; the interface roots do not publish its InferCtx, Scope, partial body state, or checked body in their results. The captured code supports this boundary design; dynamic transitive dependency exclusion and reuse are not asserted as experimentally proven by this review.

The complete associated test set has exactly one explicit TODO entry, sage_meta::todo::checking_symbol_keyed_interfaces. Its empty body has no assertions and is not functional coverage. Its comment explicitly identifies the remaining verification matrix: distinct symbol-keyed signature/body trace roots, absence of ambient caller parameters and callee-body reads, and reuse after interface-preserving edits. Accept this existing, honest test deferral: completion requires implementing that trace/edit fixture with meaningful dependency and reuse assertions. A regression introducing a transitive body read would not be detected by this placeholder today. No ordinary or N/A tests are represented, and no TODO implementation is being claimed complete. The TODO remains visible under the review decisions policy.

Commands performed: cargo meta review start/read and inspection of the captured source; cargo fmt after comment-only evidence edits. No behavioral tests were run by this reviewer, and no passing-test claim is made. Workspace build and centralized delegated Rust quality/Sage sanity checks are assigned to the coordinator. No production behavior was changed and no suspected behavioral failure was identified in this boundary inspection. All requirements are accounted for by the source design and explicit test deferral; no further edits requested.
